steps_walked.title: Cross-language search through the concept rings: the 'only the words I typed' toggle, the 40-form limit switch, the sense picker, language chips and grouping, per-form counts with one total, the stacked per-language chart, the concept map, watches and the bulletin annexe, Arabic/Chinese/Japanese search with its re-index job
prerequisites: The app is at current main, which includes S8 (merged 2026-09-25), with its dependencies reinstalled. jieba is now a core dependency (Chinese). Japanese word splitting in search also needs the optional [segmentation] extra (sudachipy); it is only needed for the optional Japanese check in N13.

PART A (steps N1–N11) runs on a THROWAWAY data folder, never your real data: a plaintext store at /tmp/oo-rowN, seeded with scripts/ui_clickthrough_seed.py plus the 9-article concept fixture docs/audit/cross-language-lens-clickthrough-2026-09-17/concept_fixture.py, and served on port 8010. The different port means its browser settings (language, analysis tabs) never mix with your real install on :8000.

Do Part A on the SAME DAY you seed. The fixture articles are dated 1–6 days before seeding. Insights → Trends (7-day window, N8) and the weekly Bulletin (the 7 days before today, N10) only see them in that week.

Start the throwaway with `.venv/bin/open-omniscience serve`. Do not use `python -m src.api.main` or `--ephemeral`: both serve an app whose Mindmap graph fails with a 500 (docs/audit/concept-map-clickthrough-2026-09-17/README.md). Use the terminal where you typed `export OO_DATA_DIR=…` ONLY for the throwaway, and start your real app the usual way.

PART B (steps N12–N13) runs on your own ENCRYPTED install, unlocked, with its real corpus. It works best if the corpus has Arabic and Chinese articles (and Japanese, for the optional check) that were collected BEFORE you updated to this version.
Before N13, make a fresh backup of the real install: the gear button 'Settings' at the bottom of the sidebar → subtab 'Data & backup' → section 'Export / Backup' → 'Export / Back up…'.

Keep airplane mode ON for the whole pass: the top-bar plane icon stays FILLED, so never click it. No step in this row sends anything off the machine, so no consent popup should appear. If one does, click Cancel and write down which click raised it.
You need a zip viewer (N10), and you need to paste Arabic and Chinese words; copy them from this sheet.

RUN: click 'Re-index search (Arabic, Chinese, Japanese)' → OK, then open the task manager and watch 'Processes' while it runs. OPTIONAL, only if the run lasts more than a minute: click the top-bar power icon 'Shut down the app' mid-run, start the app again, and click the same Settings button. When the line beside the button says it is done, click 'Search re-index report (.json)' and save the tab that opens (Ctrl+S). AFTER: analyse the same words again. Then run the re-index once more. The re-index rewrites only the search index; articles and keywords are not touched. There is no undo button, which is what the backup is for.
steps.expect: If the line says 'This store's search index has not been upgraded yet. Restart the app once, then run this again.', restart and retry. While it runs, the task manager's 'AI & analysis' group shows 'Re-indexing search for Arabic, Chinese and Japanese' (this label stays in English whatever the language) with a 'running' pill and a bar reading 'checked / total · %'. There is no Pause button there; see not_clickable. If you did the optional interruption, the confirm says 'Continue the search re-index? It resumes where it stopped (N% done).' At the end the line reads 'Articles checked: N · re-indexed: M (Arabic: a · Chinese: b · Japanese: c)', and the saved JSON shows the same figures. AFTER compared with BEFORE: the Chinese word's total is the same or higher (higher whenever older Chinese articles contain it); القاهره now gives the SAME total as القاهرة (it was lower before); climate is unchanged; 東京 rises only if the optional segmentation package is installed. The second run reports re-indexed: 0. Keep both sets of numbers and the report: they are the real-corpus before/after figures that a session must write into the PR.

Budget roughly 55 min for Part A (N1–N10), 30 min for the language pass (N11) and 25 min for Part B, plus however long the real re-index takes (it depends on corpus size). The expected numbers (160 / 156 / 'climate 156 · climat 3 …' / 'eng 3 · fra 3 …' / '40 of 44') are the ones the sandbox Chromium walks measured, or the code computes, on this exact seed plus fixture. S8 does not move them: English is not folded and no Chinese article is about climate. If yours differ, record them; what must hold is the relationships stated in each step.

Things this pass will show that are NOT your mistake. They were found while preparing and checking the sheet; record them rather than fail the step:
(1) On the throwaway, the full-text and set-based numbers (Articles list, Count each form, Search page, Sentiment: 160) and the keyword-based numbers (Trend 'By language' total, concept-map arms, Insights hover: 7) differ a lot. The seeder titles each of its 153 climate articles 'Climate coverage (edition N) — <lang>' and writes the body without the word, so 'climate' is in the title text without being an extracted keyword. The agreement probe only ever compared these on a 7-article fixture where every article carries the keyword. On a real corpus, expect the keyword-based figure to be at most the list figure. Whether that counts as 'agreement' needs your ruling.
(2) 'مناخ 0' stays at 0 after S8. Q507 folds alef, teh marbuta and yeh shapes and strips vowel marks (src/database/fts_norm.py:93-117). It does not strip the definite article ال, and the Arabic fixture writes المناخ. The lens walk README hoped S8 would fix this; that is outside what Q507 rules.
(3) The Articles list's default order is RELEVANCE (BM25), not date, although the pressed view button is labelled 'Interleave by date' (N2). Q508 = a rules 'interleaved by date'. Only 'Sort by: Date' delivers it.
(4) When a term is declined because it has several senses, the grey block still prints the caveat 'This search matched the concept in every language the ring covers…' under 'so it was not expanded' (N5).
(5) The limit sentence carries no numbers. 'expanded to 40 of 44 forms' is only readable after clicking 'Count each form', as '40 of 44 forms counted' (N5). Q503 = a words the disclosure as 'expanded to 40 of 63 forms'.
(6) The search re-index has no Pause or Resume button in either task manager, although its confirm text says it 'can be paused from the task manager', and its task-manager label is English in every language (see not_clickable and N13).
(7) The Search page ('Run the full Boolean search') uses the lens of whichever analysis window last ran in THAT browser tab, but shows no concept block and no toggle. That is why N3 runs it from the first browser tab. Its 'result(s)' line is not translated.
(8) With 'only the words I typed' on, Mindmap → Concept still draws the other languages' arms, because the concept-map request does not carry the expand flag (src/static/app-analysis.js:2031-2034). Judge whether that reads as contradicting the toggle.
(9) The set-based analysis tabs stop at 900 articles (_SQLITE_SAFE_IN_CAP). Competitive says so; Sentiment does not (N12).
(10) The Bulletin fold sits inside 'Uninstall & wipe', directly above 'Wipe everything now'. This is already known (docs/audit/ui-visual-2026-09-08/findings.csv P3, and docs/audit/13_ENCRYPTED_CLICKTHROUGH_2026-09-16.md), so take care not to press a wipe button.
(11) Also recorded, not part of row N: Devanagari and Bengali vowel signs are split in the search index (docs/ledger/OPEN_QUEUE.md).

walk.summary: The click-through clause does not close on this walk. The toggles, limit switch, sense picker, chips, per-form counts, stacked chart, concept map, watch disclosure, bulletin annexe and Arabic/Chinese re-index all behave as ruled in en, fr, ar, zh and ja on an encrypted store; on the stand-in store the re-index moved 预算 and 诊所 from 0 to 28 and the voweled Arabic spelling from 0 to 55. It fails on a P1 race where a new analysis tab shows another tab's results under its own label, a P2 sense-pin leak between tabs, and a P2 stacked-chart legend chip that cannot be clicked back; the real-install steps N12 and N13 still need the operator's corpus.

verdicts.title: A new analysis browser tab can paint another workspace tab's results under its own label (list, total, grey block, chips)
verdicts.reason: I reproduced this on my own encrypted seeded store: 462 articles, booted locked on :8832 and unlocked via #pw, airplane mode on throughout. I left the climate analysis tab open, made it the saved active tab with a real click on its strip tab, then opened 'Analysis: “election”' from the palette into a new browser tab. In 4 of 6 runs the strip and header said election while Articles showed climate's grey block, climate's chips and '160 Articles'. Run 3 had the right total (20) but climate's chips, which matches the walker's zh case. Every run showed the new election tab sending BOTH /api/articles?query=climate and ?query=election, so the tab loads twice every time. To make it deterministic I held climate's /api/articles response: election painted correctly (20, declined-sense block), then climate's late response overwrote it with 160 when released. The same overwrite happens inside one window: click the climate strip tab then the election strip tab while climate's response is slow, and the list ends up showing climate under election. So the missing stale-run guard is the core fault, and the boot double-load makes it hit on most palette searches, which open a new browser tab by design. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/walk/N-recheck/R-race.json (B_runs, C_*), R-inwin.json, shots/N-recheck-B-race-run5-en.png, N-recheck-C-race-forced-en.png, N-recheck-inwindow-race-en.png. P1 holds: results for one query are shown under another query's label with nothing on screen to say so.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:448 _anRestoreTabs() restores the saved strip. Then app-boot.js:459 showTab('analyze', false) runs, and because _anHydrated is false, src/static/app-shell.js:146-150 applies the RESTORED active tab: _anApplySeed calls loadAnalysis at src/static/app-analysis.js:178. Next, app-boot.js:474 openAnalysisFor(analyze) → _anSpawn → _anActivate → _anApplySeed starts a SECOND loadAnalysis. loadAnalysis (app-analysis.js:1961) has no run token. The un-awaited _anLoadArticles (:1831, called at :2043) and _anLoadArtFacets (:1289, called at :2044) of whichever run finishes last write the shared #an-art-list, #an-xlang and #an-art-facets, as well as the _anArtParams, _anArtFacetData and _anLastParams globals.
verdicts.suggested_fix: (1) In _hydrateCardCorpus (app-boot.js ~455-460), when ?analyze= or ?corpus= is present, set _anHydrated = true before showTab('analyze', false). The restored active tab is then not loaded, and only the deep-linked tab renders through _anSpawn → _anActivate. (2) Add a generation guard for in-window switching: `const run = ++_anRunSeq` at the top of loadAnalysis; pass it to _anLoadArticles and _anLoadArtFacets; after every await, return without writing when `run !== _anRunSeq`.

verdicts.title: A sense pin leaks across analysis tabs: new tabs open pre-pinned and carry another tab's sense in their URL
verdicts.reason: Reproduced in en; it is deterministic, not the race the walker suspected. I picked “public election” in an election tab (216 articles, and the tab's saved lens held senses {election: public-election}). I then opened 'Analysis: “climate”' from the palette in a new browser tab. Its URL became ?analyze=climate&sense=election%3Apublic-election, and the climate tab's saved lens now carries the election pin. Opening 'Analysis: “election”' in another new tab then came up already pinned: 'which you chose', 216 articles, no sense picker (the default is the declined-sense picker with 20). The literal toggle leaks the same way, which is worse. After 'Show only the words I typed' on climate, a brand-new search for 'climat' opened with ?expand=0 and 'Showing only the words you typed', 3 articles, where the default is 160. I confirmed that total with a real click on climat's own strip tab, so the race is ruled out. A related symptom: the URL's analyze= keeps the boot term while the lens of whichever tab is active is written beside it (seen: ?analyze=climat&expand=0 while the climate tab was active), so a reload or a shared link applies one tab's lens to another term. Each leaked lens is disclosed on screen with a one-click way back, so this stays P2 rather than P1. It breaks the code's own rule at app-analysis.js:164-166: 'The lens belongs to the TAB: switching between two analyses must not carry one reader's narrowing onto the other's corpus.' Evidence: R-race.json D_* and E_*; R-misc.json G_*; shots/N-recheck-D-climate-url-leak-en.png, N-recheck-D-election-prepinned-en.png, N-recheck-G-climat-literal-leak-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:459 showTab('analyze', false) applies the restored active tab. Its _anApplySeed calls _anWriteLensToUrl (src/static/app-analysis.js:168 → :1496), which writes THAT tab's sense, expand and cap into location.search. Only afterwards does app-boot.js:469 `const lens = _anReadLensFromUrl()` read the URL, so the deep-linked tab is seeded with the restored tab's lens (app-boot.js:474). _anSaveTabs then saves it into oo.an.tabs.v1, where it spreads to the next new tab.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Move `const lens = _anReadLensFromUrl();` (and the prov read) above `showTab('analyze', false)` in _hydrateCardCorpus, and skip loading the restored tab when a deep link is present (same change as fix (1) of the race). Optionally, have _anWriteLensToUrl also rewrite analyze= to the active tab's query so the URL always describes one tab.

verdicts.title: ooChart legend: hiding a series removes its chip, so it cannot be clicked back
verdicts.reason: Reproduced: Analysis climate, then Trend, then By language. The legend had eng, fra, deu, spa, ita, por, all aria-pressed=true. After one click on 'eng' it had 5 chips (fra…por), with no dimmed or aria-pressed=false chip left to click. The code clearly meant to keep hidden chips: the legend template already emits aria-pressed='false' and opacity:.4 for s.hidden, but hidden series never reach it. Invariant #16 lists 'legend chips toggle series' as ruled ooChart behaviour, and this is the shared toolkit, so every ooChart chart is affected. Evidence: R-race.json F_legend_before / F_legend_after_hide / F_dimmed_chip_present=false; shots/N-recheck-F-legend-hidden-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-markets.js:1967-1969 visible() filters out hidden series (`all.filter(s => !s.hidden)`), and the legend at app-markets.js:2253 is built from `vs = visible()`. A hidden series therefore loses its chip and its click handler.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Build the legend from `all`, computing vis per series, e.g. `legend.innerHTML = all.map((s0) => { const s = {...s0, vis: s0.pts.filter(p => p.t >= t0 && p.t <= t1)}; ... })`. The existing hidden branch (aria-pressed=false, opacity .4) then renders the dimmed chip, and a second click restores the band.

verdicts.title: Articles default order is relevance while 'Interleave by date' is shown pressed (Q508 rules 'interleaved by date')
verdicts.reason: Reproduced on climate: the Sort select value is '' ('Relevance / recency'), 'Interleave by date' has aria-pressed=true, and the first published dates run 2026-09-23, 09-22, 09-20, 09-24, 09-24, 09-25, 09-25, 2024-01-24, 2024-04-30… (bm25 order). Q508 = (a) «Interleaved by date, a language chip on every row» (RULINGS_INDEX.md:150), and the code comment at app-analysis.js:1783 says 'The ruled DEFAULT is interleaved by date', yet no code sorts by date by default. Not by-design. P2 is a borderline grade: the dates are visible on each row and 'Sort by: Date' works, but a maintainer-ruled default is unmet and a pressed control misstates the order. Evidence: R-race.json F_default_order.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-analysis.js:1846-1848 (_anLoadArticles) deletes sort_by when #an-adv-sort is '' (src/static/index.html:468 is the default option). src/api/main.py:1455-1458 then keeps FTS relevance order, which is bm25 (src/database/fts.py:937). app-analysis.js:1800 still labels that state 'Interleave by date', pressed.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Make date descending the analysis Articles default: in _anLoadArticles, when no sort is chosen and the list is not grouped, set sort_by=date and sort_dir=desc, or make 'Date' the default option of #an-adv-sort. Keep 'Relevance / recency' as an explicit choice. Alternatively, stop claiming 'by date' while the order is relevance.

verdicts.title: Watches list keeps English composite strings after a language switch until reload
verdicts.reason: Reproduced: I added a watch in en, switched to ar with the top-bar switcher, and went Trends → Watches. The row still read '≥ 2 articles within 30 day(s) · last fired: never' and 'the concept “climate”' in English, while the surrounding chrome was Arabic. After a reload it read '‏≥ 2 مقالات خلال 30 يوم · آخر تفعيل: أبدًا' and 'المفهوم «climate»'. This is the frozen-locale class that app-boot.js's oo:langchange listener fixes surface by surface; the watches panel is not in that list. Evidence: R-misc.json W_ar_no_reload vs W_ar_after_reload; shots/N-recheck-W-watch-ar-noreload.png, N-recheck-W-watch-ar-reload.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-insights.js:1313 and :1277 build the row with tf() when it renders. loadWatches runs only once per page load (showInsightCat, app-insights.js:97-105, guarded by _insLoaded), and it is not called from the oo:langchange listener at src/static/app-boot.js:41.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Add `try { if (_insLoaded.has('watches')) loadWatches(); } catch (_e) {}` to the existing oo:langchange listener in app-boot.js. Better still, re-render from a cached payload so the switch sends no request.

verdicts.title: The user's watch name is machine-translated on screen
verdicts.reason: Reproduced: a watch named 'Climate' shows as مناخ in ar, both before and after a reload. The i18n engine's header concedes that a data string matching a UI key gets translated ('rare, and harmless'). That is a code comment, not a ruling, and the project already opts user and keyword data out of the walker with data-i18n-dyn (S04-06), so this is not by-design. Evidence: R-misc.json W_ar_name_html.
verdicts.root_cause: The src/static/i18n.js:35-58 DOM walker translates any text node exactly equal to a locale key ('Climate' → src/static/locales/ar.json:2125), and src/static/app-insights.js:1305 renders the user's name in a plain <b>.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Render the name as `${esc(w.name)}` at app-insights.js:1305. Apply the same to w.query and to the history 'Watch: {name}' label.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced in ar, Insights → Trends, hovering 'climate'. The #oo-tip bubble is Arabic apart from the sentence 'Counts only, never a score. The trend ratio is noisy on a young corpus; … not a claim about the world.' The non-negotiables require every caveat string ×12. I kept P3 because this is the hover layer. Evidence: R-misc.json O_ar_hover; shots/N-recheck-O-insights-hover-ar.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-boot.js:363 appends the server caveat verbatim (`d.caveat ? ' · ' + d.caveat`) without t(), and the server prose at src/analytics/queries.py:3051-3055 has no key in any locale file.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Use `t(d.caveat)` at app-boot.js:363 and add the caveat sentence as a key in all 12 locales, as was done for the cross-language rail caveat.

verdicts.title: Airplane coachmark covers the palette results at 375 px and the sidebar's Insights item in Arabic
verdicts.reason: (a) Confirmed at 375x800 in en with a fresh profile: the coach sits at [64,108,334,281] over the first palette row 'Analysis: “climate”' [22,205,353,248], and elementFromPoint at that row's centre is #net-coach. (b) Confirmed, but only by a narrower path than the walker described. When the app boots in ar, the coach is placed at [232,8,502,143] and the Insights item [1200,159,1429,200] is clickable. When the language is switched en → ar live while the coach is showing, the coach stays at its LTR position [1162,62,1432,198] over the now right-hand sidebar. The topmost element at the Insights item is the coach's own 'Not now', and Playwright's click was blocked. No consent breach: 'Go online' still routes through ensureOnline, and 'Not now' only dismisses. Evidence: R-coach.json 375_palette_row0 and ar_insights_nav; R-coach-ar.json; shots/N-recheck-375-palette-coach-en.png, N-recheck-coach-after-switch-ar.png.
verdicts.root_cause: _placeCoach (src/static/app-core.js:1017) runs only when the coach is shown and on window resize (app-core.js:1085-1087), never on oo:langchange, so a live dir flip leaves the coach at its LTR spot. #net-coach has z-index 360 (src/static/app.css:1803), above the command palette.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Call _placeCoach() from the existing oo:langchange listener in app-boot.js. Hide the coach non-permanently while the palette is open (e.g. dismissNetCoach(false) in the palette's open path), or put it below the palette's z-index.

verdicts.title: Search page result line is not translated
verdicts.reason: Reproduced in Français: the palette row 'Lancer la recherche booléenne complète pour “climat”' opens the Search page, whose #search-meta reads '160 result(s) (showing 50)'. Evidence: R-misc.json N_fr_search_meta; shots/N-recheck-N-search-fr.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-analysis.js:2314-2315 builds the line from a hard-coded English template literal (`${data.total} result(s)` + ` (showing ${n})`) with no t() or tf(). The results table header on the next line is also hard-coded ('Title', 'Source', 'Published', 'Lang'), though the DOM walker may cover those single words.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Use tf('{n} result(s)', {n}) and tf('(showing {shown})', {shown}), with keys added in all 12 locales (a similar 'showing {shown} of {total}' key already exists).

verdicts.title: Concept map ignores 'Show only the words I typed'
verdicts.reason: Reproduced: with the literal toggle on (156, 'Showing only the words you typed'), Mindmap → Concept still draws all six arms (eng 3 · fra 3 · deu 1 · spa 1 · ita 1 · por 1) and nothing says the view ignores the toggle. I found no ruling asking for this. Q501 rules one lens for every tab, and Q512 only rules the tree's shape, so this is not by-design. P3, because the Concept view is by nature a picture of the ring. Evidence: R-misc.json I_*; shots/N-recheck-I-concept-literal-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-analysis.js:2029-2034 builds the concept-map request with only ui_lang, literal_cap and sense (expand is not forwarded), and src/api/insights.py:1805-1807 hard-codes resolve_concept_keywords(..., expand=True).
verdicts.suggested_fix: When _anExpand is false, show one keyed line on the Concept view, e.g. 'The Concept view shows the whole ring; the list is showing only the words you typed.' Or hide the Concept button while literal is on. Forwarding expand=false would make the endpoint return expanded:false and drop the view entirely.

verdicts.title: Disclosure wording: ring caveat under a declined term, and a limit sentence with no numbers
verdicts.reason: Reproduced both parts. (a) election's block reads 'election denotes several concepts, so it was not expanded…' and directly below it 'This search matched the concept in every language the ring covers, not only the words you typed.' That sentence is false for this search. (b) After picking “public election” the rail says only 'The search was widened to the most-mentioned forms only. Turn the limit off…', with no numbers. The /api/articles payload does carry searched_forms=40 and total_forms=44 for the term. Q503 = (a) rules the disclosure as «expanded to 40 of 63 forms», and on screen the figure appears only after the lazy 'Count each form' click. Evidence: R-misc.json J_election_block, K_pinned_block, K_payload_cap_fields; shots/N-recheck-K-limit-sentence-en.png.
verdicts.root_cause: (a) src/analytics/equivalence.py:901-904: disclosure() always emits the expansion caveat, even when only a decline or a pin-miss made the block 'interesting'. src/static/app-analysis.js:1640-1643 renders `cav` unconditionally. (b) app-analysis.js:1618-1621 renders only cross.cap_caveat and never the per-term searched_forms / total_forms.
verdicts.suggested_fix: (a) Render the caveat only when cross.expanded, or emit it server-side only when any_expanded. (b) In the capped branch, add a keyed tf('expanded to {searched} of {total} forms', …) built from the capped terms' searched_forms and total_forms.

verdicts.title: Small i18n and grammar slips on this row's surfaces
verdicts.reason: Reproduced in zh: the election block reads 'election 指代多个概念，因此未做扩展. 搜索其中之一：', with an ASCII '. ' after a translated frame. The code puts the same period after ja. In en, Group by language on climate gives the heading 'spa 1 articles'. Evidence: R-misc.json M_zh_election_block; R-coach.json group_headings_climate; shots/N-recheck-M-election-zh.png.
verdicts.root_cause: src/static/app-analysis.js:1598-1599 adds a literal '. ' outside the translated tf() frame. app-analysis.js:1826 uses t('{n} articles').replace('{n}', n) with no singular form.
verdicts.suggested_fix: Move the sentence-final punctuation into the keyed frame so each locale supplies its own (e.g. '。' in zh and ja), and add a '{n} article' key for n === 1, or use the project's plural helper if it has one.
